I have to say, I'm surprised I don't see more people playing this! I had to get used to the crazy flashy graphics, but the game itself if addictive. I have yet to be able to join a multiplayer game, because there are never any listed! But I've run through many, many times solo and although in the very beginning it feels very monotonous, as you unlock guns and figure out the skill points it becomes easier and more fun!
The controls are easy enough, and it doesnt take you long to really get into the swing of things. The enemy types are split and spread out enough that it gives you a new sense of danger in each zone instead of a full rinse repeat you would see in other games like this. I just finished my first final boss kill last night, and I really enjoyed it as well as most of the other boss fights!
The first of the 2 problems I have with the game are the invisible boundaries of objects (if you try to shoot over something that only goes up to your ankles on your character, it will still stop the shot even at that height. As well as trying to shoot around light poles, doesn't work.) It makes it extremely difficult to take out pillar humping enemies from a distance, and the levels with 2 floors at the same time are just plain annoying because you cant shoot anything above you unless they are right up against a rail. The second problem is description. It is hard to tell what each gun has and each skill unless you memorize them by the picture. While this is fine and just takes a bit, I find it trite and obnoxious because I have TBI and it's hard for me to remember everything all the time, especially about something so simple on a game!

Either way, great job studio, the games legit!

Moderately recommended. Let's say 6 / 10. TLDR : competently done, nothing groundbreaking here, could use faster metaprogression.

- Visuals : the aesthetics is gorgeous. If like me you're a sucker for that vaporwave / neon drenched style, you cannot skip this game. Calling it "cyberpunk" is a bit of stretch though, it's certainly "cyber" but there is very little "punk" to be found. Need I remind y'all that the cyberpunk genre is not just pretty lights and robots, it's also a criticism of our society through exaggerated dystopia ? But hey, even a game called "Cyberpunk" was very light on it, so I'll give it a pass. The artistic direction, while not especially revolutionnary, is coherent.

- Performance : Ran like a charm on my previous rig, stills runs like a charm on the new one. Of course, it would be a pity if it ran worse on newer hardware, but hey, it happens. Old specs : Ryzen 5 2600X / RTX 2600 Super / 16 GB of RAM / everything on SSD / Screen resolution 1920x1080@60Hz. New specs : Ryzen 7 5800X / RTX 360 TI / 32 GB of RAM / still everything on SSD / Screen resolution 3440x1440@75Hz. Never a single FPS dip, in any case. The game may not revolutionize the genre, but at least it won't give you a headache. It's sad that those days we must count it as a positive, but yeah, this game works as it should right out of the metaphorical box.

- Gameplay : Now this is where I won't only have nice things to say.

The controls are fine, you might need to rebind them if you're not on a QWERTY board (like yours truly), but aside from this, they are intuitive and responsive. As they should be, but again, that's the kind of things worth mentionning those days. If you get hit in the face, it won't be because you were fighting the controls, it was because you ♥♥♥♥♥♥ up. [i]Git gud[/i]

This being a roguelike, there is a meta progression. Each run brings its benefits. [i]So. Very. SLOWLY ![/i] Sure, I myself needed to [i]git gud[/i], no doubt there, but man, after 8 runs I still hadn't finished the first zone, my stats were still mostly ♥♥♥♥♥♥. I found the game a tad bit too hard, so I played in easy, hoping to get further, but "easy" is questionably easier, because it does reduce your "nanites" gain... Nanites are the currency you spend to upgrade your skills, so basically they are the metaprogression. I'll be honest, I cheat engined my nanites, and could unlock about 1/3 of the metaprogression. Didn't want to go overboard. The next run was attempted in normal, and I basically cheesed most of it. At this point, bosses became a joke.. Once you are strong enough, bosses won't be a danger anymore. Nope, the things that will kill you the most are actually the regular mobs.

So, about the runs themselves. You begin by chosing your class among 2, then 3 once you reached a certain point (and the very reason why I cheated : I wanted to play that class NOW, not in 10 or 20 more runs).

As for the classes, Soldier has a shield and a big hammer. Some upgrades, due to their nature, work best with him. Like the automissile that shoots every interval.

Ninja is actually a solid defensive class, because every time you activate stealth, even for a split second, you break line of sight for the enemies, which also resets they attack animlation they have. The problem is, it prevents ANY animation. Enemies no longer even move, it seems to remove all AI from the game, even the one you need. Like the aforementionned auto-missiles. I've tried using them with ninja, but they simply are useless. I never stay out of stealth long enough for them to fire, and it seems their timer resets too. If per chance they were to fire, the moment I entered stealth, they lost their target and merely flew in a straight line.

Hacker is my most recent unlock, have barely scratched the surface, but... He needs a different way to cast his hacks. Time doesn't slow down at all when you start casting, so you'd need an extra pair of hands to keep moving and dodging while selecting the right hack for the right job. Or maybe I just need to [i]git gud[/i].

Once you pick your class, it's time to pick the gun (guns if you have spent enough nanite to unlock secondary) among the ones you have unlocked. To unlock a gun, you need to kill stuff with it. Problem is, some weapons are only found rather late, so to unlock them, you need... Yeah, more runs. 250 kills or more is basically nothing for a gun you find in the very first minutes of a run, but it's not true anymore when you find it late. In my last run, I lasted much longer than usual, killed a metric ton of stuff with the plasma bow, but I still need to kill some. Welp, guess I'll play again, using the reliable but uninspired assault riffle / shotgun combo unbtil I find those plasma bow and disc launcher again and pray that I kill enough stuff before dying this time...

I mean, those are pretty standard mechanics for a roguelike, but damn, they feel overstretched here.

Then, well, into the city to kill ♥♥♥♥. You enter an area, stuff spawns, then another wave, then a third wave. Then the area is secure, which leaves you time to pick loot, look for hidden crates (which are rather frequent-ish early on, but terribly scarce  later on). While the visuals are stunning, the level design is... Meh. You could maybe use the environment to your advantage if those pesky mobs didn't spawn far too close. It's always some corridors of a kind or another, a few spots to take cover, many destructible things that deal damage when they explode, and that's it. Once you've looted what you could / cared for, move on to the next area, rince and repeat. After a few of those (3 ? 4 ?), you reach a gate that takes you to the next level, and can chose an uprgade among 4 randomly offered. After repeating that process 7 (I think 7 anyway) times, you fight a big bad, which is rather easily cheesed through (maybe not in the first few runs), then move on to the next biome.

This is a long process. Very long. Unless you die, of course. Good thing you can leave to the main menu and save, else you'd simply wish you die so you can take care of the laundry or whatever. Sometimes, you have things to do, you know. And because of the structure of the game, it gets repetitive. The enemies change depending on the biome, but there aren't really new mechanics introduced, save for the weapons. Between level design, annoying enemy mechanics and lack of variety, it can get tedious to get rid of them all, and I mean that quite litteraly. It's not dangerous so long as you don't ♥♥♥♥ up, but it gets repetitive, and so you pay less attention, and ♥♥♥♥ up.

Still, this game is in no way bad. I insisted more on the bad things because I believe it's important to be aware of them, but overall, the game is enjoyable. In moderate sessions at a time. If you're mostly interested in frantic action with pauses in between, competently done, then look no further. If you want a more substantial meta progression and greater variety, this may not be the game for you.

Dat aesthetics, tho !
solid game once things start ramping up
